# English Language Learners Stack Exchange

> > Community-driven Q&A platform for non-native English speakers learning grammar, vocabulary, usage, and idiomatic expressions.

English Language Learners Stack Exchange is part of the Stack Exchange network, providing expert answers to questions about English grammar, prepositions, word usage, pronunciation, and language conventions. The site serves learners seeking clarification on confusing aspects of English, from modal verbs to idiomatic expressions.

## Key Topics

- Prepositions
- Word usage and meaning
- Grammar (tenses, modal verbs)
- Gerunds vs infinitives
- Frequency expressions
- Pronunciation and phonetics
- American English vs British English
- Possessives and articles
- Reflexive pronouns
- Idiomatic expressions
- Word requests and vocabulary
- Time expressions
- Verb tenses (past perfect, simple past)
- Stack Exchange community guidelines

## Grammar and Usage Questions

- [Difference between will and shall](https://ell.stackexchange.com/questions/124164/difference-between-will-and-shall): Q&A explaining modal verb differences between 'will' and 'shall' in modern English
- [Past perfect vs past tense confusion](https://ell.stackexchange.com/questions/102567/im-confusing-with-past-perfect-and-past-tense): Q&A on understanding past perfect vs simple past tense usage in news articles
- [Usage of 'a something' in sentences](https://ell.stackexchange.com/questions/118613/usage-of-a-something-in-the-sentence): Q&A on metalinguistic usage of indefinite articles with 'something/nothing'
- [A patients guide or A patient's guide](https://ell.stackexchange.com/questions/133174/a-patients-guide-or-a-patients-guide): Q&A on possessive apostrophe usage in guide titles: patient's vs patients

## Prepositions and Phrasal Constructions

- [Once a year vs once in a year](https://ell.stackexchange.com/questions/103371/do-once-a-year-and-once-in-a-year-mean-the-same-thing): Q&A on preposition usage in frequency expressions: 'once a year' vs 'once in a year'
- [Time to myself vs time for myself](https://ell.stackexchange.com/questions/116063/difference-between-having-time-to-myself-and-having-time-for-myself): Q&A comparing reflexive pronoun usage with 'to' vs 'for' prepositions
- [Guide someone on how to do something](https://ell.stackexchange.com/questions/325555/is-it-correct-and-natural-to-say-guide-someone-on-how-to-do-something): Q&A on preposition choice with 'guide': 'guide on' vs 'guide through' usage
- [A guide to finding vs a guide to find](https://ell.stackexchange.com/questions/77866/a-guide-to-finding-a-guide-to-find): Q&A on gerund vs infinitive choice after 'guide to' in titles

## Pronunciation and Spelling

- [Fruit vs Build vs Ruin vs Guide pronunciation](https://ell.stackexchange.com/questions/112264/fruit-vs-build-vs-ruin-vs-guide-difference-in-pronunciation): Q&A explaining pronunciation variations of 'ui' phonogram in English words

## Vocabulary and Word Requests

- [Describing an aggressive person in AmE](https://ell.stackexchange.com/questions/114631/how-would-you-describe-an-aggressive-guy-who-tends-to-fight-people-most-of-the-t): Word request for describing aggressive behavior in American English slang
